0.0.n: A polite way to address the whole audience.

0.2.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.4.n: This is the speaker’s name, written in katakana.

0.5.n: A polite sentence ending; the speaker leaves out 私は because the context makes it clear.

1.0.n: Combines with から to give the starting day.

1.1.n: Marks the starting point in time.

1.2.n: An English loanword written in katakana.

1.3.n: Marks the podcast as what the speaker is starting.

1.4.n: スタート combines with する to form a verb; します is its polite form.

2.0.n: Sets the time frame for this first episode.

2.1.n: は sets the topic, while ね adds a friendly, conversational touch.

2.3.n: Describes the beginning of the series and reinforces １回目.

2.4.n: Connects 最初 to １回目 so the first expression describes the second.

2.5.n: 回 counts occurrences, and 目 makes the count an ordered position; here it refers to an episode.

2.6.n: The linking form of だ used after a noun before ので.

2.7.n: Introduces the reason for what the speaker will explain next.

3.0.n: Limits how much the speaker plans to say.

3.1.n: Combines with のこと to refer broadly to the speaker as a topic.

3.2.n: Connects 私 to こと in the expression 私のこと.

3.3.n: In 私のこと, こと makes the speaker’s personal details the topic.

3.4.n: Joins personal information and activities as the two topics.

3.6.n: Identifies the person doing the activities.

3.7.n: Marks 私 as the person performing やっている.

3.8.n: やる becomes やっている to describe ongoing involvement; this phrase describes 活動.

3.9.n: Refers to the projects or work the speaker is involved in.

3.10.n: Marks the topics the speaker will discuss.

3.11.n: The prefix お adds politeness; お話をする means to speak about something.

3.12.n: Marks お話 as the noun paired with します.

3.13.n: Polite form of する; together with お話を, it expresses giving a talk or explanation.

4.0.n: Introduces another topic the speaker plans to discuss.

4.1.n: Directly describes ポッドキャスト and must be followed by a noun.

4.2.n: Refers to the show the speaker is introducing.

4.3.n: Links the podcast to its purpose.

4.4.n: Names the next topic; the sentence continues in the following line.

5.0.n: Points back to the podcast’s purpose mentioned in the previous line.

5.1.n: Connects これ to the planned discussion.

5.2.n: Adds the podcast’s purpose to the topics already listed.

5.3.n: お話しする becomes お話ししたい with たい, expressing the speaker’s desire.

5.4.n: Adds a reflective, gentle tone to the speaker’s wish.

5.5.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

5.6.n: Polite form of 思う; here it softens the expression of what the speaker wants to do.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when introducing yourself; a name plus です is enough.

1.lit: From today, I will start a podcast.
1.tip: から marks when something begins, so 今日から means starting today.

2.lit: As for today, you know, since it is the first, first episode,
2.tip: After a noun, use なので to give a reason: since it is that thing.

3.lit: A little, about things concerning me and activities I am doing, I will give a talk.
3.tip: 私がやっている comes before 活動 to describe it: activities that I am doing.

4.tip: This line names a topic without finishing the sentence; これ in the next line refers back to it.

5.lit: About this too, I think I would like to talk.
5.tip: たいなと思います expresses a wish gently rather than making a firm announcement.
